pairs: Invenitur autem in descriptionibus Jeremiæ prophetæ,
Now it is found in the descriptions of the prophet Jeremiah that he ordered those who transmigrated to take the fire,
quod jussit eos ignem accipere qui transmigrabant,
And he gave them the law,
so that they would never forget the commandments of the Lord,
and so that they would not go astray in their minds,
seeing the idols of gold and silver,
And in this manner, with other sayings,
hortabatur ne legem amoverent a corde suo.
he exhorted them, lest they remove the law from their heart.
Furthermore, it was in the same writing,
quomodo tabernaculum et arcam jussit propheta divino responso ad se facto comitari secum,
how the prophet, by divine response, ordered that the tabernacle and the ark be made to accompany him,
usquequo exiit in montem in quo Moyses ascendit, et vidit Dei hæreditatem.
until he exited from the mountain, where Moses ascended and saw the inheritance of God.
Jeremiah found a place in a cave.
And he brought both the tabernacle,
and the altar of incense into that place,
And certain ones of those who followed him,
qui sequebantur, ut notarent sibi locum:
approached to make note of the location,
but they were not able to find it.
But when Jeremiah knew of it, he blamed them, saying:
Quod ignotus erit locus donec congreget Deus congregationem populi, et propitius fiat:
until God shall gather together the congregation of the people, and until he may be favorably inclined.
And then the Lord will reveal these things,
and the majesty of the Lord shall appear,
and there will be a cloud,
just as it was also manifested to Moses,
et sicut cum Salomon petiit ut locus sanctificaretur magno Deo, manifestabat hæc.
and just as he manifested these when Solomon petitioned that the place should be sanctified to the great God.
For he also drew upon wisdom magnificently,
he offered the sacrifice of the dedication and the consummation of the temple.
Sicut et Moyses orabat ad Dominum,
et descendit ignis de cælo et consumpsit holocaustum,
just as Moses prayed to the Lord,
and fire descended from heaven and consumed the holocaust,
et descendit ignis de cælo et consumpsit holocaustum.
so also Solomon prayed and fire descended from heaven and consumed the holocaust.
Et dixit Moyses: Eo quod non sit comestum quod erat pro peccato, consumptum est.
And Moses said that it was consumed because the sin offering was not eaten.
et Salomon octo diebus celebravit dedicationem.
Solomon also celebrated the eight days of the dedication.
Inferebantur autem in descriptionibus et commentariis Nehemiæ hæc eadem:
Moreover, these same things were put into the descriptions and commentaries of Nehemiah, including how,
et ut construens bibliothecam congregavit de regionibus libros et prophetarum et David,
when constructing a library, he gathered together from the regions the books of the Prophets, and of David,
and the epistles of the kings,
et Judas ea quæ deciderant per bellum quod nobis acciderat,
Judas also gathered together all the things that were destroyed by the war that befell us,
Therefore, if you desire these things,
send those who may carry them to you.
And so, since we will be celebrating the purification, we wrote to you.
and has rendered to all the inheritance,
just as he promised in the law,
will quickly have mercy on us
et congregavit de sub cælo in locum sanctum.
and will gather us together from under heaven into the holy place.
Eripuit enim nos de magnis periculis,
For he has rescued us from great perils,
and he has purged the place.
and the purification of the great temple,
and the dedication of the altar,
sed et de præliis quæ pertinent ad Antiochum Nobilem et filium ejus Eupatorem,
and also about the battles, which pertain to Antiochus the illustrious, and his son, Eupator,
et de illuminationibus quæ de cælo factæ sunt ad eos qui pro Judæis fortiter fecerunt,
which came from heaven to those who acted on behalf of the Jews with fortitude,
vindicated the entire region and put to flight a multitude of the barbarous,
et famosissimum in toto orbe templum recuperarent,
and recovered the most famous temple in the whole world,
et civitatem liberarent, et leges quæ abolitæ erant,
and freed the city, and restored the laws that were abolished.
Domino cum omni tranquillitate propitio facto illis.
with all tranquility, was acting favorably toward them.
Itemque ab Jasone Cyrenæo quinque libris comprehensa tentavimus nos uno volumine breviare.
And similar things as have been comprised in five books by Jason the Cyrenean, we have attempted to abridge into one volume.
For, considering the multitude of the books,
et difficultatem volentibus aggredi narrationes historiarum propter multitudinem rerum,
and the difficulty that those who are willing to undertake the narrations of histories find, due to the multitude of events,
we have taken care, so that, indeed,
those who are willing to read may have delights of the mind,
the studious may more easily be able to commit it to memory,
and also so that all readers may find it useful.
qui hoc opus breviandi causa suscepimus,
who have taken up the task of abridging this work,
immo vero negotium plenum vigiliarum et sudoris assumpsimus.
in truth, more correctly, we have assumed an activity full of vigilance and sweat.
Just as those who prepare a feast also seek to be attentive to the will of others,
et quærunt aliorum voluntati parere propter multorum gratiam,
for the sake of the gratitude of many,
Veritatem quidem de singulis auctoribus concedentes,
Indeed, leaving to the authors the truths about particular details,
ipsi autem secundum datam formam brevitati studentes.
we instead have been devoted to this form, striving to be brief.
Sicut enim novæ domus architecto de universa structura curandum est;
For, just as the architect of a new house will have concern for the entire structure, and,
ei vero qui pingere curat, quæ apta sunt ad ornatum exquirenda sunt:
in truth, he who takes care to paint it will seek out what is fitting to adorn it,
ita æstimandum est et in nobis.
so also should such things be considered by us.
et curiosius partes singulas quasque disquirere,
and to discuss every particular point attentively,
is the duty of the author of a history.
Yet truly, to pursue brevity of speech,
and to shun the extension of matters,
Therefore, here we will begin the narration.
Let so much be sufficient to say in preface.
Stultum etenim est ante historiam effluere,
For it is foolish to go on and on before the account,
when the account itself is succinct.
